title: Surrey man dies in hospital after collapsing in RCMP custody
subtitle: Pepper spray, baton used to subdue man
article: A man who collapsed after being arrested by police in south Surrey two days earlier died Thursday in hospital, RCMP said.
The man was identified as David James Stitt, 46, of Surrey, B.C.
Cpl. Dale Carr, of the RCMP's integrated homicide investigation team, said in a news release issued Thursday that an autopsy will be conducted to determine the cause of death.
The RCMP received a call about a "disturbance" in the 13500 block of Crescent Road near the Nicomekl River shortly after midnight Tuesday, Carr said.
The first officer who arrived at the scene found a man in "an agitated state." As the officer tried to calm him down, a violent struggle ensued, Carr said.
An RCMP news release issued Wednesday said the female officer did not use any weapons during the altercation, but Carr said Thursday that pepper spray and a baton were used to subdue the man.

"As the male moved toward the officer with a stick in hand, the officer deployed pepper spray. The male continued to advance toward the officer and engaged in a physical altercation with her," Carr said.
"The officer ... [then] deployed her defensive baton, striking the male in the lower body."
An area resident and a person driving by the scene came to the aid of the officer, Carr said.
When a second officer arrived, the man was arrested and placed in handcuffs, Carr said. The man collapsed while being escorted to a police vehicle, he added.
Shane Brown told CBC News that Stitt was a gentle person known to friends as Painter Dave.
Brown, who said he's known Stitt for 15 years, said his friend was stressed about work, but didn't do drugs and only drank socially.
"What happened?" Brown said. "What took my friend, who was the most calm, passive man? What took him from calm and passive to raging and out of control?"

The homicide investigation team took over the investigation Wednesday night. Carr said at the time the man was apparently involved in "a couple of encounters" with motorists on Crescent Road earlier Tuesday evening.
That part of the investigation continues, Carr said Thursday.
